Good evening, ladies and gentlemen and may I welcome you to the Astoria Theatre. Tonight’s film, “The Longest Day” is the third in this week’s series of twelve films about human relationships. This is the second time we’ve run a film series and I’m sure it will be as popular as the first one.
“The Longest Day” is a moving film about a father’s struggle to deal with his son’s illness. For 24 hours the father doesn’t know if his sonwill live or die. The film which runs for 120 minutes will break even the hardest heart.
After the film we invite you to a cheese and wine reception and you will have the chance 
to talk to both the director and some of the actors.

A substance called tuberculin is injected into the skin on the forearm to find out whether or not there are tuberculosis bacteria present in the body.
